bib.title: WaveNet: A Generative Model for Raw Audio

question: Can autoregressive neural generative models, successful on images and text, generate wideband raw audio waveforms (at least 16,000 samples per second)?
hypothesis: Dilated causal convolutions give a large enough receptive field to model raw audio autoregressively, and this yields more natural speech than parametric and concatenative TTS.
contributions: WaveNets generate raw speech with subjective naturalness never before reported in TTS, as assessed by human raters.
New architectures based on dilated causal convolutions with very large receptive fields.
A single model conditioned on speaker identity generates different voices.
The same architecture gives strong results on a small speech recognition dataset and is promising for music.

method.summary: A fully convolutional autoregressive model of raw audio: stacked dilated causal convolutions with gated activations, residual and skip connections, and a 256-way softmax over mu-law quantised samples. It is trained by maximum likelihood, with global (speaker) or local (linguistic features, log F0) conditioning, and evaluated on multi-speaker generation, TTS (human MOS and paired preference), music and TIMIT.
method.task: autoregressive raw-audio generation (TTS, multi-speaker speech, music) and TIMIT phoneme recognition

datasets.name: CSTR VCTK
datasets.preprocessing: speaker ID fed as one-hot vector

datasets.name: Google North American English TTS database
datasets.split: 100 test sentences not in training data
datasets.source: single professional female speaker; Google TTS system data
datasets.preprocessing: 16 kHz, 8-bit mu-law; linguistic features every 5 ms by phone-level forced alignment

datasets.name: Google Mandarin Chinese TTS database
datasets.split: 100 test sentences not in training data

datasets.name: MagnaTagATune
datasets.preprocessing: tags cleaned by merging similar tags and removing those with too few clips

models.name: WaveNet
models.architecture: dilated causal convolution stack, gated tanh/sigmoid units, residual + skip connections, softmax over 256 values
models.context: receptive field about 300 ms (multi-speaker), 240 ms (TTS), several seconds (music)

other.local_conditioning_upsampling: transposed convolutions (learned); repeating values worked slightly worse
other.TIMIT_head: mean-pooling to 10 ms frames (160x downsampling) then a few non-causal convolutions

other.sampling: trained at 22.05 kHz, synthesised at 16 kHz via Vocaine resampling

models.name: F0 and duration predictors
models.architecture: LSTM-RNN phone duration; autoregressive CNN log F0 (200 Hz)

training.objective: maximise log-likelihood of next-sample categorical distribution; TIMIT adds a frame-classification loss alongside next-sample prediction

other.validation: hyperparameters tuned on a validation set (sizes not given)

inference.decoding: ancestral sampling, one sample at a time, each fed back as input

metrics.name: MOS naturalness
metrics.definition: 5-point Likert (1 Bad to 5 Excellent), 8 raters per stimulus

metrics.name: Paired preference
metrics.definition: listeners choose preferred sample or neutral; 8 raters per pair

metrics.name: PER
metrics.definition: phoneme error rate on TIMIT test set

eval.protocol: Blind, crowdsourced, paid native speakers; each subject up to 8 (English) or 63 (Mandarin) stimuli; ratings without headphones (about 40%) excluded; 100 test sentences; p values in Table 2.

results.setup: North American English TTS, 24.6 h single female speaker, 100 held-out test sentences, crowdsourced MOS, 8 raters per stimulus; WaveNet conditioned on linguistic features and log F0
results.table: Table 1, row WaveNet (L+F), column North American English

results.claim: WaveNet (L+F) beats the best baseline in Mandarin MOS.
results.setup: Mandarin TTS, 34.8 h, 100 test sentences, WaveNet (L+F)
results.table: Table 1, row WaveNet (L+F), column Mandarin Chinese

results.claim: Natural 16-bit PCM English speech MOS, the ceiling.
results.setup: North American English TTS, 24.6 h single female speaker, 100 held-out test sentences, crowdsourced MOS, 8 raters per stimulus
results.table: Table 1, row Natural (16-bit linear PCM), column North American English

results.setup: North American English TTS, 24.6 h single female speaker, 100 held-out test sentences, crowdsourced MOS, 8 raters per stimulus
results.table: Table 1, row HMM-driven concatenative, column North American English

results.claim: WaveNet narrows the gap to natural speech by 51% (English) and 69% (Mandarin).
results.setup: English and Mandarin TTS as above; gap measured against natural speech (16-bit for English)
results.quote:
The gap in the MOSs from the best synthetic speech to the natural ones decreased from 0.69 to 0.34
(51%) in US English and 0.42 to 0.13 (69%) in Mandarin Chinese.
results.note: Mandarin natural 8-bit mu-law (4.25) exceeds 16-bit (4.21) in Table 1.

results.claim: TIMIT phoneme error rate with joint next-sample and frame-classification loss, best from a raw-audio model to the authors' knowledge.
results.setup: TIMIT test set, mean-pooling to 10 ms frames, two loss terms
results.quote: achieved 18.8 PER on the test set

results.claim: Multi-speaker model covers all 109 VCTK speakers; adding speakers improved validation performance over a single speaker.
results.quote:
adding speakers resulted in

results.claim: Receptive field of about 300 ms limits long-range coherence in speech: model remembers the last 2-3 phonemes.
results.quote: receptive ﬁeld (about 300 milliseconds), which means it can only remember the last 2–3 phonemes

results.claim: With a 240 ms receptive field and linguistic features only, WaveNet sometimes stresses wrong words; adding F0 conditioning fixed this.
results.quote:
the size of the receptive ﬁeld of the WaveNet, 240

a

limits: No hyperparameters for training (optimizer, learning rate, batch size, steps, layers, channels, parameter count, hardware) are stated.
Sampling is sequential, one step per audio sample, so generation is slow; speed is not reported.
Receptive field of 240-300 ms is too short for prosody and phoneme-level coherence without F0 conditioning; music lacks long-range consistency.
Music evaluation is subjective listening only; no quantitative metric.
Evaluation is on single-speaker datasets and 100 sentences; about 40% of ratings dropped for no headphones.

terms.definition: a convolution where the filter is applied over an area larger than its length by skipping input values with a certain step, made causal so predictions depend only on past samples
a single latent representation h that influences the output distribution across all timesteps
a second timeseries ht, possibly at lower sampling frequency, upsampled and used in the activation unit
